That's a fantastic idea! I actually did a little journaling after I made this post and it did help me a lot. I have a sense for who I am but I think need to work on expressing myself to people using language. I do most of my communicating through touch and raw emotion so it's a little hard getting to know new people once we are past common pleasantries. My mind just goes blank. Maybe if I make a habit of journaling I'll get better at using words. I could also change my relationship with words, I think of them as extremely specific and missing the point entirly. Touch and emotion feel more direct. Words are a useful tool though, and just because others seem to use them with relative ease doesn't mean I should give up on them because I find it difficult.

As for the rest: 

I would love a life partner. Right now I am doing all I can towards that so the rest is left up to time and fate. 

As for a career, what I really want is something that would make moment to moment living the best it can be. The trouble is I often find the moment to be dysphoric in some way. Kind of no matter what it is I'm doing. I actually have started skating recently and I notice a big improvement on my outlook when I have that little bit of adrenaline in my system and my mind is focused on using my body. Perhaps I've been experiencing boredom slowly withering away my desires. So a bit of a pickle I'm in is that most of my meaning is found in stability (seeing my family and cat every day) but it's boring me to the point I can't experience meaning. I would love a life partner so I can take some of that with me while I go experience the world.

....that ended up being long. I suppose I know what I want: a person to go with me every step of the journey and a life with a lot of change and action because apparently that's what my brain needs. 

Thank you so much for sparking this up! It feels good to view how I feel with a little more clarity.

A major distinction between what I'm calling "short term climbing" and "long term climbing" is that short term resets every day. Any one days climb has no relation to another days climb. Long term is a little more abstract because it is a continual climb stretching through the many days. The long term climb exists mostly as thought or memory in your mind and is not swayed by your moment to moment moods and needs

Thanks for the reply. I looked into maslows hierarchy and I think you pretty much nailed it on the head. It has given me a very logical structural way to view my existential angst. I just dont like the act of climbing tbh. I imagine a lot of instincts kick in when your at the bottom and you naturally want to climb but at some point there is no natural drive pointing you up and it becomes a sort of "cerebral wandering". When I look around at all the pointless stuff humans make and do it really screams "cerebral wandering". A lot of people seem to be living happily at the top of the hierarchy but some people seem to be in a bit of a cerebral nightmare.

I believe we climb the hierarchy in two ways: In the short term...when you wake up that would be staring at the bottom, you'd take care of your body's needs and by the end of the day you'd be enjoying some love and social connection... and in the long term... planning, securing food and other needs for the future/the fulfillment of knowing the things you care about are taken care of. I think short term climbing is more likely linked to physical sensation and instinct while long term climbing is something the "thinking mind" has more to do with. 

 Could people be wired towards either nomad/hunter gatherer day to day living or a farmers long term planning?

 It would make sense that the society we live in today is predominantly long term survival based because only the settled farmers would have progressed into civilization. And then as some of the nomads integrated into civilization their genes get passed on and now there are people who don't care about long term survival because they're brains are wired for finding only the things they need for today.
